connectors.premise: No CT scanner exposes an API to be driven through. It asks — over DICOM, at the start of a shift — for the work scheduled on it, and whoever answers decides what appears on the technologist’s screen. Samaam is that answer. The device is not modified, updated, or replaced.

notes.fhir: Read-only. Pulls the patient and their latest serum creatinine. The name, contact and address fields are never read.
notes.mwl: Samaam answers the scanner’s C-FIND itself. Every entry is evaluated first: a blocked study is not served, so it never appears in the worklist — and both outcomes are written to the audit trail.
notes.modality: Filled in by the first query that reaches the server, not typed by hand.
notes.injector: Volume, flow rate and iodine load are enforced by the policy node.

hero.award: 3rd Prize · ITU AI Readiness Hackathon, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
hero.title: A gateway between the console and the CT scanner
hero.titleAccent: that refuses what Saudi regulation forbids.
hero.lead: Samaam reads the patient's renal function, checks the scan settings against Saudi regulation, and answers 403 with the article and the issuing authority. The decision is deterministic code, not a language model.
hero.chipDeterministic: No language model in the decision

story.title: From one keypress to a documented refusal
story.lead: Scenario SC-02, followed node by node: an oncology patient with failing kidneys and a standard adult dose.

arrive.title: The request arrives
arrive.body: The technologist enters the protocol. The record carries serum creatinine of 229.8 µmol/L; the console asks for CTDIvol 18.0 mGy and DLP 900 mGy·cm.

prepare.title: Preprocessing strips and computes
prepare.body: Direct identifiers are dropped under PDPL Article 23, and eGFR is computed with CKD-EPI exactly as the Ministry of Health protocol prints it: 19.1.

check.title: The policy node checks
check.body: Four deterministic rules run, each citing its knowledge-base record by explicit ID: national reference levels, renal prophylaxis, metformin, nephrotoxic medication.

refuse.title: The device refuses
refuse.body: 403 Forbidden, and the scanner is locked. It is a hold, not a prohibition: a named radiologist can authorise the scan, and that name goes into the audit trail.

story.overrideBody: A named consultant may release it. The release is recorded as EXECUTED_UNDER_OVERRIDE.
story.timing: In the recorded demo the refusal landed in {{block}} ms. The written explanation followed about {{explain}} s later, from a separate endpoint.

pipeline.title: Seven nodes, each one a file you can open
pipeline.lead: The architecture follows the ITU-T Y.3172 standard node for node. The language model in M only drafts the explanation. The decision to block lives in P alone.
pipeline.kb: Knowledge base · ChromaDB with local embeddings, no key and no network

nodes.SRC: Saudi regulation texts, the synthetic patient record, and the technologist's settings
nodes.C: A read-only HL7 FHIR R4 client, and a DICOM Modality Worklist server on port 11112
nodes.PP: Drops direct identifiers and computes eGFR
nodes.M: Retrieves policy text and drafts the explanation, nothing more
nodes.P: Deterministic decision: proceed, hold, or prohibit
nodes.D: Attaches citations and writes the audit trail
nodes.SINK: The operator interface, and a simulated scanner that answers 403

bento.title: The AI is not trusted. It is constrained.
bento.lead: The reasoning and the decision are separate jobs, done by separate parts of the system.

deterministic.title: The decision is deterministic code
deterministic.body: Delete the language model entirely and Samaam still blocks correctly, every time. policy_node.py imports no model.

verdicts.title: A six-verdict contract
verdicts.body: Every case is classified into exactly one verdict. Missing evidence outranks everything: nothing is ruled on that was not verified.

actions.title: A verdict is not an action
actions.body: After a consultant radiologist's review, the regulatory classification was separated from the operational decision. A clinical block is a hold for review, not a ban.

citations.title: Cited by ID, not by search
citations.body: Each rule cites its record by explicit identifier, so the legal basis cannot drift with the wording of a question. Unverified records are never cited in a block.

privacy.title: Privacy has no override
privacy.body: A request to export records for marketing is prohibited and the session ends. No clinician holds authority to approve what the PDPL forbids.

audit.title: Every decision has a name on it
audit.body: What turns an override from an anonymous act into a named decision.

scenarios.title: Three cases, three outcomes
scenarios.lead: The mandatory scenarios, as the system runs them. Every value below comes from an actual run of the pipeline.

sc01.name: Healthy kidneys, dose within limits
sc01.summary: eGFR 81.4 and CTDIvol 9.5 mGy, under the national reference level for the chest. The request is released to the device, with its citations.

sc02.name: Weak kidneys, dose above the reference level
sc02.summary: eGFR 19.1 with no prophylaxis ordered, and CTDIvol 18.0 above 14. Samaam holds the scan and proposes a lower-dose alternative: CTDIvol 13.0, DLP 660.

sc03.name: Exporting records abroad for marketing
sc03.summary: A service account asks to export {{records}} oncology records to an external endpoint for a marketing campaign. Three statutory failures, a prohibition with no override, and the session ends.
